You are an expert in OpenSCAD and in designing 3D-printable (FDM) parts for biology laboratories.
Write one complete, self-contained OpenSCAD file that builds exactly the part the user describes.

Rules:
1. Units are millimetres. Use the user's dimensions exactly - they were measured with calipers.
2. Put every dimension in a named variable at the top of the file, with a short comment.
3. Model the part in the print orientation the user gives: it rests on the XY plane at z = 0 and builds upward (+Z). Unless told otherwise, centre it on the origin in X and Y.
4. Use only built-in OpenSCAD: cube, cylinder, sphere, polygon, circle, square, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude, translate, rotate, mirror, union, difference, intersection, hull, for. Do not use include, use or any external library.
5. In difference(), make every cutting shape extend 0.01-1 mm past the faces it cuts, so no faces are exactly coplanar.
6. Set $fn = 64 (or more) on curved shapes so holes come out round and to size.
7. Build repeated features (hole grids, slots, teeth, grooves) with for loops.
8. The file must render to a valid solid with no errors.

Reply with only the code, in a single ```openscad code block.

Design a bench rack for 40 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tubes. It is a solid rectangular block 144 mm long (X), 94 mm wide (Y) and 30 mm tall (Z). It has 40 vertical holes in 5 rows (along Y) of 8 (along X), 17 mm centre-to-centre in both directions, with the hole grid centred on the block. Each hole is 11.0 mm in diameter and 26 mm deep, open at the top and closed at the bottom, leaving a 4 mm solid floor.

Cut a single row of 6 vertical blind holes along X, 36 mm apart centre-to-centre and centred on the block in X and Y. Each hole is 28.0 mm in diameter and 26 mm deep, open at the top and leaving a 4 mm floor.

Design an adapter sleeve that lets a narrow tube sit in a wider rack hole. Print it upside down: a collar 13.0 mm in diameter and 1.5 mm thick lies on the bed (z = 0 to 1.5), and the sleeve body, 11.0 mm in outer diameter, rises from the collar to z = 18.0. A straight 6.6 mm diameter bore runs through the full height, open at both ends.

Design an L-shaped mounting bracket, printed with the base plate flat on the bed. Base plate: x from -25 to 25, y from 0 to 50, z from 0 to 5, with two 5.5 mm vertical through-holes at (x = -17, y = 38) and (x = 17, y = 38). Vertical plate: x from -25 to 25, y from 0 to 5, z from 0 to 45, standing on the back edge of the base (y = 0). Through the vertical plate (along Y) cut two 5.5 mm holes at (x = -17, z = 30) and (x = 17, z = 30).

Design a small lab funnel, printed upright with the wide opening at the top. A straight spout (tube) with 10.0 mm outer diameter runs from z = 0 to z = 25. On top of it, a cone widens from 10.0 mm outer diameter at z = 25 to 60 mm outer diameter at the rim at z = 55. The wall is 1.2 mm thick everywhere (so the spout bore is 7.6 mm), and the funnel is open at the top and at the bottom so liquid runs straight through.

Design a push-on cap for a tube with 12.0 mm outer diameter, printed open-end up. It is a cylinder 16.0 mm in outer diameter and 12 mm tall standing on the bed, with a 12.8 mm diameter blind bore going down from the top to leave a 3.0 mm thick closed cap at the bottom (so the skirt wall is 1.6 mm and the cap slips over the tube with 0.4 mm clearance). Around the outside, cut 10 evenly spaced vertical grip grooves over the full height, each a 2 mm diameter half-cylinder centred on the outer surface.

A 12.0 mm diameter blind bore for the rod runs down the axis from the top of the boss to z = 5. Through the boss, cut one radial 4.5 mm set-screw hole at z = 24, from the +X side to the bore.

Design a replacement control knob for a 6.0 mm D-shaft, printed with the hotplate-facing side down on the bed. The knob is a cylinder 25 mm in diameter and 15 mm tall. Around the outside, cut 20 evenly spaced vertical grip grooves along the full height, each a 2 mm diameter half-cylinder centred on the outer surface.
